objectives: Strategic Management defines the scope or spheres within which decisions can be taken by the subordinates in an organization. This course is designed as the capstone course taken by all business students during their final year of study. In the current business environment characterized by rapid change and global competition, this lecture aims at introducing the business environment under the light of the strategic concepts and processes. Topics covered include strategic management, social responsibility, environmental and internal analysis and diagnosis, strategy selection, and implementation and evaluation.
content:
PART I: The Logic of Strategic Analysis Introduction: What Is Strategy? Firm Performance and Competitive Advantage Evaluating Environmental Threats Evaluating Environmental Opportunities Evaluating Firm Strengths and Weaknesses

PART II: Business Strategies Cost Leadership Product Differentiation Flexibility: Real Options Analysis Under Risk and Uncertainty Tacit Collusion: Cooperation to Reduce Competition

PART III: Corporate Strategies Vertical Integration Strategies Diversification Strategies Implementing Corporate Diversification Strategic Alliances Merger and Acquisition Strategies International Strategies
